object_context: Child of H4d1a. Fix a smooth projective complex family f:X->S, a rational Hodge-locus branch T through s0, and a chosen algebraic central witness z0 for a flat rational Hodge class alpha. Determine exactly what is certified by first-order branch obstruction annihilation delta_1|_{T_{s0}T}=0 (equivalently, under the exact witness-moduli tangent-obstruction interface, branch tangent directions lift over dual numbers), and test whether that first-order condition can serve as a certificate of formal witness domination of T. This remains conditional on initial algebraicity of z0 and is not a root Hodge-conjecture atom.
structural_coordinates: root coefficient scope is rational and the ambient fibers are smooth projective complex varieties
the atom begins with a chosen algebraic central witness; it cannot establish initial algebraicity of an arbitrary rational Hodge class
the witness category and coefficient bookkeeping must be fixed before interpreting tangent or obstruction maps
write q:W->S for a source-controlled local witness/incidence parameter space when such a space exists; branch tangent liftability is a statement about T_{s0}T relative to im(dq_{w0})
delta_1|T=0 is a first-order/dual-number condition and does not by itself assert lifts across arbitrary small Artin extensions
formal witness domination requires an all-order infinitesimal lifting property or equivalent completed-local/functorial statement, not merely a tangent-space inclusion
Hodge loci carry natural analytic-scheme structure and can be nonreduced; reduced support can therefore hide higher-order nilpotent structure
special complete-intersection and divisor cases can close variational Hodge statements using extra smoothness/dimension/incidence geometry that is absent in arbitrary higher codimension
formal lifting remains separate from algebraization, monodromy/global continuation and domination on a global Hodge-locus component
singular or nonreduced branch structure must be treated scheme-theoretically rather than replaced by its reduced set
equivalent_formulations: test whether every Hodge-branch tangent vector has a chosen-witness lift over Spec(C[epsilon]/(epsilon^2)), while keeping higher-order lifts explicitly unresolved
compare the tangent map of a witness/incidence space q:W->S with the tangent space of the registered Hodge-locus branch T, then separately ask whether q is formally smooth or Artin-surjective over T
compare completed local deformation functors of the chosen witness locus and Hodge branch rather than treating equality of reduced supports or tangent spaces as all-order equality
express the successor obligation as lifting along every relevant small extension A'->A of local Artin C-algebras after the first-order obstruction has vanished
solved_analogues: complete-intersection cycles on hypersurfaces where variational Hodge is proved using special incidence geometry and Hodge-locus calculations
smooth/formally smooth morphisms, where infinitesimal lifting across all square-zero or small extensions is the governing all-order condition rather than one tangent-space calculation
near_solved_analogues: Noether-Lefschetz/Hodge loci for combinations of intersecting linear spaces, where reduced loci can agree while the Hodge locus is nonreduced or singular

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A Jacobian or linearized controllability calculation can certify behavior for infinitesimal perturbations while higher-order nonlinear constraints remain. A controller is not declared globally or formally capable solely because the linearized map covers the desired tangent directions.
common_abstraction: first-order reachable directions versus all-order reachable states
linearized map versus nonlinear deformation law
local tangent coverage as a necessary but not generally sufficient certificate

desired infinitesimal direction -> tangent vector in T_{s0}T
higher nonlinear compatibility -> lifting through higher Artin extensions
reachable-state certificate -> formal witness domination of the Hodge branch
